title: Height map of a solid built from unit cubes (3 rows, 3 columns)
bodyMd: A solid is made of identical unit cubes standing on a floor grid of 3 rows and 3 columns. Each number in the table is the count of cubes stacked on that square of the grid; 0 means the square is empty. Row 1 is nearest to an observer standing in front of the solid, and Column 1 is on the observer's left. Each stack rests on the floor with its cubes directly on top of one another. Every cube face has an area of one square unit.

data.caption: Number of unit cubes stacked on each square of the floor grid. Row 1 is nearest to the observer; Column 1 is on the observer's left.

accessibilityText: A table of cube counts with three rows and three columns, describing a solid made of unit cubes. Each number is how many cubes are stacked on that square of the floor; zero means the square is empty. The rows run from front to back and the columns from left to right. Row 1, the front row: 2, 1, 0. Row 2, the middle row: 1, 3, 1. Row 3, the back row: 0, 1, 2. In total there are 11 cubes standing on 7 non-empty squares. The two empty squares are at the front right and the back left corners.

provenance.notes: Original invented height map. 11 cubes on 7 squares; every row and column of the table rises and falls at most once.
